claims.text: What the image looks like Buzzword: Codman triangle / sunburst periostitis on bone X-ray → osteosarcoma
claims.quote: Codman triangle / sunburst periostitis Bone X-ray Osteosarcoma

claims.text: Example knee radiograph: a destructive osteosarcoma in the femur above the knee with a lytic destructive appearance and a classic Codman's triangle showing pathologic periosteal elevation
claims.quote: This radiograph of the knee shows a destructive osteosarcoma in the femur above the knee with a lytic destructive appearance and a classic Codman's triangle showing pathologic periosteal elevation.

claims.text: Findings on imaging studies vary and may include sclerotic or lytic features
claims.quote: Findings on imaging studies vary and may include sclerotic or lytic features.

claims.text: Periosteal osteosarcoma (more of a cartilage matrix surface tumor that also contains bone matrix, and malignant) is often located on the mid-shaft femur and appears as a sunburst on radiograph
claims.quote: Periosteal osteosarcoma is more of a cartilage matrix surface tumor that also contains bone matrix and is malignant. It is often located on the mid-shaft femur and appears as a sunburst on radiograph.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Site: usually around the knee (distal femur more often than proximal tibia) or in other long bones, particularly the metaphyseal-diaphyseal area; may metastasize, usually to lung or other bone
claims.quote: Osteosarcoma usually develops around the knee (distal femur more often than proximal tibia) or in other long bones, particularly the metaphyseal-diaphyseal area, and may metastasize, usually to lung or other bone.

claims.text: Patients need a chest CT for lung metastases, a nuclear medicine whole-body bone scan for bone metastases, and MRI of the entire involved extremity for metachronous lesions ("skip lesions"); PET-CT may show distant metastases or metachronous lesions as well and is an evolving staging modality
claims.quote: Patients need a chest CT to evaluate for lung metastases and a nuclear medicine whole-body bone scan to evaluate for bone metastases. MRI is done of the entire involved extremity to evaluate for metachronous lesions (or "skip lesions"). PET-CT may show distant metastases or metachronous lesions as well and is an evolving staging modality.

claims.text: Causes Produces malignant osteoid (immature bone) from tumor bone cells
claims.quote: Osteosarcoma produces malignant osteoid (immature bone) from tumor bone cells.

claims.text: The most common malignant primary bone tumor (if myeloma is considered a marrow cell tumor and not a primary bone tumor), and highly malignant; most common in children and teenagers, although it can occur at any age
claims.quote: Osteosarcoma is the most common malignant primary bone tumor (if one considers myeloma a marrow cell tumor and not a primary bone tumor) and is highly malignant. It is most common in children and teenagers, although it can occur at any age.

claims.text: Two peaks of incidence: highest in adolescents and very young adults (coinciding with the adolescent growth spurt), and a secondary peak in older adults (≥ age 60), especially those with risk factors such as Paget disease, bone infarcts, and bone previously exposed to high-dose radiation therapy for another cancer many years earlier
claims.quote: There are 2 peaks of incidence; incidence is highest in adolescents and very young adults (coinciding with adolescent growth spurt) and secondary peak occurs in older adults (≥ age 60), especially in those with risk factors such as Paget disease, bone infarcts, and areas of bone previously exposed to high-dose radiation therapy for another cancer many years earlier.

claims.text: Children who carry the gene for hereditary retinoblastoma (RB1 variants) and Li-Fraumeni syndrome (TP53) are at higher risk
claims.quote: Children who carry the gene for hereditary retinoblastoma (variants of RB1 gene) and Li-Fraumeni syndrome (TP53 gene) are at higher risk of developing osteosarcoma.

claims.text: Symptoms Pain, swelling/mass, and loss of joint motion are the usual symptoms
claims.quote: Pain, swelling/mass, and loss of joint motion are the usual symptoms.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Chemotherapy plus surgery; adjuvant chemotherapy increases survival from < 20% to > 65% at 5 years for patients presenting with localized disease
claims.quote: Treatment of osteosarcoma is a combination of chemotherapy and surgery. Use of adjuvant chemotherapy increases survival from < 20% to > 65% at 5 years for patients presenting with localized disease (1).

claims.text: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy begins before surgical resection, to treat the early micrometastatic disease assumed to be present even if it is not seen on staging imaging
claims.quote: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy begins before surgical resection. The goal is to treat the early micrometastatic disease assumed to be present even if it is not seen on staging imaging studies.

claims.text: Surgery aims to resect the tumor en bloc (with all surrounding reactive tissue and a rim of normal tissue) to avoid microscopic spillage; if a negative margin cannot be achieved with limb-salvage surgery, amputation should be considered
claims.quote: The goal of surgery is to resect the tumor—including all surrounding reactive tissue and a rim of surrounding normal tissue—en bloc, to avoid microscopic spillage of tumor cells. Necrosis and surgical margins are critically important to the patient's outcome. If a negative margin cannot be achieved with limb-salvage surgery, amputation should be considered.

claims.text: More than 85% of patients can be treated with limb-sparing surgery without decreasing the long-term survival rate
claims.quote: More than 85% of patients can be treated with limb-sparing surgery without decreasing the long-term survival rate.
